fact: PolyTurf's manual says larger damaged areas may need the damaged piece cut out and a new piece inserted; straight cuts are easier, curved random sides are less noticeable, and an irregular cut-out can be traced on paper and transferred to the back of new turf with directional grain aligned the same way.
quote: Larger areas may require the offending piece to be cut out and a new piece inserted. Cut out the damaged piece, straight edges are easier, but curved, random sides will be less noticeable. If you do random shaped cutouts, place the cutout piece on a piece of newsprint or other paper and trace the outline on it. Then transfer the outline to a new piece of turf (on the back), making sure the turf is aligned the same way for directional grain turf. Note: Make sure you transfer it the right way, you don’t want a mirror image after you cut it out!
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping, Repairs (p. 13)
notes: Read in the PDF on 2026-09-25 (pdftotext). A manufacturer's DIY manual, not a standard; the page says 'the manual', never that NoCo repairs this way.

fact: For turf laid loose on its base, PolyTurf's manual joins a patch with short sections of seam tape glued on one side and slipped under the existing edge all around, then adhesive on the exposed tape, the new piece pressed down, and infill to the same density as the surrounding turf; turf glued to a slab needs no tape.
quote: If the existing turf is just laid down on the underlay, use the seam tape in short sections to join the edges of the new piece to the existing one. Place adhesive on one side of the tape and slip it under the edge of the existing turf. Do this all around the edge. Spread adhesive on the exposed tape and carefully place the new piece into position, pressing it down firmly onto the tape. Fill the new turf to the same density as the surrounding turf with the infill material. If the existing turf is glued to the substrate, then the tape is not necessary, just glue the new piece in place.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping, Repairs (p. 13)

fact: PolyTurf's manual says small, noticeable tears can be sewn together with UV-resistant, rot-proof thread.
quote: Small tears can be repaired by sewing the edges together if they are noticeable. Use a UV resistant and rot proof thread.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping, Repairs (p. 13)
notes: Firestone's code says turf seams are taped or glued and not sewn (firestone-fdc-16.6.4-turf-specs); the page sets the two side by side and hedges on whether the town line reaches a repair.

fact: PolyTurf's manual says strong acids or other chemicals can discolor its turf, and sharp objects, vehicles or vandals may damage it.
quote: While the turf is highly resistant to most normal contaminants and use, strong acids or other chemicals can discolor it, and sharp objects, vehicles, or vandals may damage it.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping, Repairs (p. 13)

fact: PolyTurf's manual advises keeping the scraps left over from the original installation to patch areas that are damaged later.
quote: It’s always a good idea to keep the scraps left over from your original installation. They can be used to patch any areas that become damaged.
source_label: PolyTurf, Installation and Maintenance Instructions: Synthetic Grass for Landscaping, Repairs (p. 13)
notes: The manual repeats it after the infill step: "NOTE: Save any leftover pieces in case you need to repair a damaged area in the future".

fact: Shaw's ShawGrass installation guidelines trim a roll's edge starting two tuft rows in for seam strength, and keep cuts as close as possible without touching, with no more than 1/8 inch between them.
quote: C. When trimming selvedge, begin cutting two tuft rows in from edge in order to achieve proper seam strength. … F. Make all cuts as close as possible without touching. Seam spacing should be no more than 1/8 inch.
source_label: Shaw Industries, ShawGrass Installation Guidelines (PDF), 5. Lay Turf
notes: Written for seaming rolls on a new install; the page applies it to a patch's edges and says so.

fact: Shaw's guidelines say some turf adhesives need flashing time for vapors to escape, which can depend on temperature and humidity; the turf edges go onto the adhesive without burying fibers in it, and the seam is weighted with sandbags or rolled once the adhesive has tacked up.
quote: Depending on the type of adhesive used, you may need to allow time for vapors/gases to escape (flashing). Refer to the adhesive manufacturer’s directions. The flashing time required may be dependent on ambient temperature and humidity. D. After adhesive has flashed, lay the edges of each roll of turf directly onto the adhesive/tape, making sure not to bury any turf fibers into the adhesive. E. Add weight (i.e. sandbags) down the length of the freshly laid seam, or use a heavy roller along the seam length once the adhesive has tacked up.
source_label: Shaw Industries, ShawGrass Installation Guidelines (PDF), 6. Seaming
notes: The section number is read from the guide's column order (5. Lay Turf precedes the seaming steps, 7. Infill Installation follows).

fact: Integriturf's installation guide says most turf has a grain that leans one way, and pieces seamed together without the same grain direction show a color difference and visible seams.
quote: Most turf products have a grain that leans in one direction. … Note: whenever two or more sections of turf are to be seamed together, you must maintain the same grain direction across all pieces. If you seam sections together without keeping the consistent grain direction you will notice a color difference and seams will be visible.
source_label: Integriturf, Synthetic Turf Installation Guide (PDF)

fact: Integriturf's installation guide names reflection from nearby windows, vinyl fencing or other reflective surfaces as a cause of melted turf fibers, and warns that gas trimmers and hedgers set down while hot will melt the turf.
quote: Another common concern would be UV reflection from nearby windows, vinyl fencing or other reflective surfaces that could cause the synthetic turf fibers to melt. Be careful to no set any hot tools or other items on the turf which could potentially damage the turf. … Power tools such as gas trimmers and hedgers have a carburetor that can get extremely hot; setting these tools down on the turf while hot will melt and damage the turf fibers.
source_label: Integriturf, Synthetic Turf Installation Guide (PDF), Pre-Installation Due Diligence
notes: "to no set" is the source's typo, kept verbatim. The same passage puts polyethylene's melting point at "around 200 degrees"; the page does not repeat that figure.

fact: SYNLawn's DIY guidelines align the rows of joined turf pieces in the same direction with equal spacing between fiber rows, cross-brush seams in both directions to make them less visible, and warn that non-professional installations can leave seams more visible.
quote: With the turf sections side by side, make sure all of the rows are aligned in the same direction. • Try to maintain equal spacing between the fiber rows. … Note: The seaming process can be tricky. Professional installers are trained to hide seams so they are almost invisible. Please be aware that non-professional installations could result in more visibility to the seams. … The turf seams should be cross-brushed in both directions. This will make the seams less visible.
source_label: SYNLawn, DIY Installation Guidelines for SYNLawn Artificial Grass (PDF posted with the product listing)

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council tells buyers to get confirmation that seams will be bonded with an industrial adhesive formulated for synthetic grass with proven weather resistance, a product usually not found in home supply stores.
quote: Confirmation that an industrial adhesive formulated for synthetic grass installations and with proven weather resistance, a product usually not found in home supply stores, will be used to bond the synthetic grass seams. The adhesive should provide a strong, hazard-free, and durable bond between adjacent synthetic grass panels or sections. It should be water, fungus, and mildew resistant, and applied by an experienced, professional installer;
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013)

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council advises buyers to keep the turf sample they select and compare it with the product delivered before installation.
quote: Keep the synthetic grass sample you select, and compare it before installation to the product that is delivered.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013)
notes: The same advice is in does-artificial-turf-fade.stc-keep-sample; this page uses it for matching a later patch.

fact: SRW Products tells users of its turf adhesive to peel back a seam just before applying adhesive, because turf backing can heat up and expand and leave gaps at seams when it cools.
quote: Peel back seam just before applying adhesive to tape. The turf backing can heat up and expand, leaving unwanted gaps at seams when the turf cools.
source_label: SRW Products, Seams Right Turf Adhesive, instructions and user tips

fact: SRW Products says to protect turf glued with its Seams Right adhesive from rain, water and freezing conditions for 12 hours, from light foot traffic for 12 hours and from heavy foot traffic for 24 hours.
quote: Protect turf from rain/water and freezing conditions for 12 hours after installation. Protect from light foot traffic for 12 hours, and heavy foot traffic for 24 hours.
source_label: SRW Products, Seams Right Turf Adhesive, instructions (Curing)
notes: One product's label; other adhesives differ. The same page's minimum surface temperature belongs to visible-seams-in-artificial-turf (editor note), so this page does not print it.

fact: SRW Products' instructions for its turf adhesive say surfaces must be flat and completely dry, above a minimum temperature, and clean of dust, loose fibers, moisture or frost for proper adhesion.
quote: For proper adhesion surfaces must be flat, completely dry, and above 40°F. Make sure the surfaces being bonded are clean of any materials that may prevent proper adhesion like dust, loose turf fibers, moisture, or frost.
source_label: SRW Products, Seams Right Turf Adhesive, instructions (Clean Surface)
notes: The page prints only 'dry surfaces' and 'a minimum temperature'; the 40°F figure and cold-weather limits belong to visible-seams-in-artificial-turf (editor note).

fact: Smart Turf's published terms say slight color variation from lot to lot, and color change over the life of the product, are common and expected.
quote: Slight variation in color from lot to lot and color changes over the life of the product is common and to be expected. This is not grounds for a warranty claim.
source_label: Smart Turf, published terms page (General Terms and Conditions)

fact: Smart Turf's published terms exclude accidents, vandalism, abuse, negligence, cuts, burns and neglect, and turf melted by reflection from Low-E windows or other localized heating.
quote: This Warranty Does Not Cover : Melted or damaged turf caused from reflection by Low E windows or any other producer of sun magnification, localized heating, or extreme heat. … Accidents, vandalism, abuse, negligence, cuts, burns or neglect.
source_label: Smart Turf, published terms page ("This Warranty Does Not Cover")

fact: SYNLawn's residential terms exclude melting from light reflected by Low-E windows and damage caused by vehicular traffic, vandalism, abuse, negligence or neglect.
quote: Additionally, this Warranty specifically excludes: 3.5 Fiber shrinkage and melting due to exposure to reflective light from Low E Rated windows and other reflective objects … 3.6 Damages caused by vehicular traffic, vandalism, abuse, negligence or neglect, normal wear and tear and Acts of God.
source_label: SYNLawn, Residential Statement of Terms and Conditions (effective 01/01/2024), sections 3.5 and 3.6

fact: K9Grass, a pet-turf maker, says most turf is tufted, with each blade a loop through the backing, which leaves it open to a dog grabbing one end and pulling it out, and that this is how dogs end up chewing artificial grass.
quote: Most turf products are “tufted” which means the blade is just a loop through the backing. This leaves it vulnerable to a dog grabbing one end and pulling it out — and this is how dogs end up chewing on artificial grass.
source_label: K9Grass (ForeverLawn), Do pets chew dog friendly turf?
notes: A maker selling a knitted pet turf; the page uses only its description of tufted turf.

fact: Firestone's development code says artificial turf areas may not contain holes, tears, seam separations or heat degradation, and damaged or worn areas must be repaired or removed and replaced so the result looks consistent with the existing turf.
quote: iii. Artificial turf areas shall not contain weeds, holes, tears, stains, discolorations, seam separations, uplifted surfaces, heat degradation, depressions, odors, excessive wear, or similar deformities and measures of deterioration. Damaged or worn areas shall be repaired or removed and replaced in manner that results in consistent appearance with the existing artificial turf.
source_label: Firestone Development Code 16.6.4.F.2.f.iii (codified through Ord. No. 1072, Dec. 10, 2025)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 through Municode's content API (product 18062, job 488870); the library page is script-rendered. F.2.a.i says maintenance of artificial turf areas shall comply with the FDC. Whether it reaches turf installed before the section was adopted is not stated; the page hedges.

fact: The Colorado Climate Center describes large day-to-night temperature changes, a thin atmosphere that lets more solar radiation through, and intense high-elevation sunlight.
quote: There are large seasonal swings in temperature and large day to night changes. … The thin atmosphere allows greater penetration of solar radiation and results in pleasant daytime conditions even during the winter. Outdoor work and recreation can often be carried out in relative comfort year round, but sunburn and skin cancer is a problem due to the intense high-elevation sunlight.
source_label: Colorado Climate Center (Colorado State University), Climate of Colorado

fact: The EPA says UV intensity increases about 6% per kilometer of elevation above sea level.
quote: UV intensity increases about 6% per kilometer elevation above sea level.
source_label: U.S. EPA, Learn About the UV Index
